Business goal: Create a durable top-level user-facing module record for the web app hierarchy.
User outcome: A privileged root operator can create a new business-facing module that later owns module-root pages and planner-visible hierarchy branches.
Notes / constraints: Module ids must be stable machine keys rather than mutable labels. The first slice is root-operated only, but the entity shape should remain compatible with future tenant-visible readers. System-managed fields are never client-supplied.
Tenant context rule: root-operated hierarchy capability outside tenant-scoped authorization; no tenant context applies
Explicitly denied roles: tenant actors; unauthenticated callers; authenticated root users without the governing capability
Authorization summary: Only privileged root operators may create top-level hierarchy modules in the first slice.
Authz scope type: exact create over one new module
Frontend visibility rule: No frontend surface is required in the first backend foundation slice.
Backend enforcement rule: Root auth and root authorization must run before module creation. Validate stable ids normalized labels lifecycle state and ordering, and reject client-supplied system-managed fields.
Session / expiry behavior: Uses existing authenticated root-session expiry rules. No tenant session behavior applies.
Request contract: Body includes webAppModuleId displayName optional businessOwnerKey optional description status and sortOrder. Client cannot supply createdAt or updatedAt.
Response contract: Returns created module detail with webAppModuleId displayName normalizedDisplayName optional businessOwnerKey optional description status sortOrder bootstrapSource=null createdAt and updatedAt.
Error contract: 400 invalid payload or rejected system-managed fields; 401 unauthenticated; 403 unauthorized; 409 duplicate module id or normalized name.
Cross-feature seams: Feeds resolved hierarchy tree and planner-selectable module catalogs for downstream `pageShellPlanning` and later route-generation consumers.
Indexes / uniqueness: Primary key on module id. Recommended unique active normalized module-name rule plus indexes on status and sort_order.
Search / filter model: Exact create only; no broad search surface in this capability.
Compatibility / migration notes: Stable module identity should survive display-name changes and later tenant-visible readers without redesigning the durable contract.
Authorization enforcement layer: Root auth middleware plus root authorization enforcement and feature-local validation.

Audit requirement: Audit successful creates and denied attempts with actor rootUserId module identifiers and selected lifecycle metadata.
Privacy / personal data impact: Low; stores internal information architecture metadata only.
Standards impact: ASVS authorization and input-validation relevance with anti-drift importance because modules become durable platform truth for downstream planners.
Acceptance notes: A privileged root operator can create one durable top-level module with stable identity validated lifecycle and stable ordering.
